**[PART II --- OTHER INFORMATION]{.underline}**

**[Item 1. Legal Proceedings]{.underline}**

On September 5, 2024, a purported securities class action lawsuit was filed against the Company and certain of its officers, Marcus R. Benton, the Company's Chief Executive Officer, and Priya Sundaram, the Company's Chief Financial Officer, in the United States District Court for the Western District of North Carolina, Case No. 3:24-cv-01847. The complaint alleges violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 related to alleged misstatements about the Company's Specialty Coatings segment revenue recognition practices. The complaint was filed on behalf of a putative class of investors who purchased the Company's common stock during the alleged class period and seeks unspecified damages, attorneys' fees, and costs.

The Company believes the claims are without merit and intends to vigorously defend against the lawsuit.

In addition to the foregoing, the Company is involved in various routine legal proceedings incidental to the conduct of its business. The Company does not believe that any of these routine matters will have a material adverse effect on its financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.

**[Item 1A. Risk Factors]{.underline}**

There have been no material changes from the risk factors previously disclosed in Part I, Item 1A of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, except as set forth below.

**Risks Related to the Integration of PolyShield**

The success of our acquisition of PolyShield Composites LLC depends, in part, on our ability to integrate the acquired business in a timely and efficient manner and to realize the anticipated strategic and financial benefits of the transaction. Integration activities may be more difficult, time-consuming, or costly than expected and may divert management's attention from our existing operations. We may encounter challenges relating to systems integration, internal controls, retention of key employees, customer relationships, operational alignment, procurement coordination, and cultural integration. If we fail to effectively integrate PolyShield or if we are unable to achieve the anticipated synergies, margin benefits, or growth opportunities associated with the acquisition, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.

**Risks Related to the Securities Class Action Litigation**

We and certain of our officers are defendants in a purported securities class action lawsuit. Securities litigation is inherently uncertain and can be expensive and time-consuming to defend, regardless of the merits of the claims asserted. Adverse outcomes may include monetary damages, settlement costs, defense expenses, diversion of management time and attention, reputational harm, and the potential for additional litigation or regulatory scrutiny. Even if we are successful in defending the claims, the costs of doing so and the distraction to management could adversely affect our business and operating results.

**Macroeconomic and Market Risks**

Our business may continue to be affected by adverse macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, elevated interest rates, supply chain disruptions, labor constraints, and foreign currency volatility. Increases in the cost of raw materials, energy, transportation, and labor may pressure margins if we are unable to fully offset such increases through pricing actions, productivity gains, or other mitigation strategies. Customer demand may also be affected by broader economic weakness, changes in industrial production, lower build rates in key end markets, or reduced capital spending by our customers. In addition, higher interest rates may increase our borrowing costs and reduce financial flexibility. Any of these factors could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.

# Each finding: (id, area, title, severity, location, issue, requirement, fix, owner)
F = []

A='A. Filing Deadline and Filing Logistics'
add(A,'Target filing date of November 14, 2024 is after the statutory due date; Veterans Day premise is wrong','Critical',
 'Transmittal e-mail (Nov. 4, 2024); Exhibit Checklist header row 3 and Filing Metadata tab (B14, B15); Q2 excerpt packet reference data',
 'The 40th day after September 30, 2024 is Saturday, November 9, 2024. Monday, November 11, 2024 is Veterans Day, a federal holiday on which the SEC is closed and EDGAR does not accept filings. The due date therefore rolls to Tuesday, November 12, 2024. The working papers state that EDGAR is open on Veterans Day and that November 11 is the deadline, and the Company is targeting Thursday, November 14, 2024, which would be two business days late. The XBRL vendor delivery date of November 12 (Checklist row 20) leaves no margin even for the correct due date.',
 'Form 10-Q, General Instruction A.1(a) (40 days after quarter-end for large accelerated filers); Exchange Act Rule 0-3(a) (due date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or federal holiday moves to the next business day); Regulation S-T Rules 12 and 13 (EDGAR business days and hours; federal holidays excluded). Consequences of a late filing: loss of Form S-3 eligibility under General Instruction I.A.3(b) for 12 months (affects the effective shelf, File No. 333-270815) and of well-known seasoned issuer status (Securities Act Rule 405); Rule 144(c)(1) current public information; NYSE Listed Company Manual Section 802.01E. A Rule 12b-25 notification (Form 12b-25 due by November 13, 2024; 10-Q then due by Monday, November 18, 2024) is available only if the delay could not be eliminated without unreasonable effort or expense, which a scheduling preference does not satisfy.',
 'Reset the target filing date to no later than Tuesday, November 12, 2024. We recommend targeting Friday, November 8, 2024, with November 12 kept as the fallback. Require the XBRL vendor to deliver final Inline XBRL files and test filings by November 6-7. Correct the Statutory Deadline entry in the Filing Metadata tab and the target date in the Checklist header. Plan for the Audit Committee and Ridgeline sign-off to fit this schedule. Notify us right away if any item in this memo cannot be cleared by November 11, so that a Form 12b-25 strategy can be evaluated before November 13.',
 'Company (Legal/Finance); XBRL vendor; Hargrove')

B='B. Cover Page and Table of Contents'
add(B,'Cover page states the wrong fiscal period','Critical','Cover page, period line',
 'The cover reads \"For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2023\". The report covers the quarter ended September 30, 2024. The error would also carry into the dei:DocumentPeriodEndDate cover-page XBRL tag.',
 'Form 10-Q cover page; Regulation S-T Rule 406 and Item 601(b)(104) of Regulation S-K (cover page data must be tagged accurately); compare Q2 2024 10-Q cover (\"June 30, 2024\").',
 'Change to \"For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2024\". Instruct the XBRL vendor to confirm DocumentPeriodEndDate = 2024-09-30, DocumentFiscalPeriodFocus = Q3 and DocumentFiscalYearFocus = 2024.','Hargrove / XBRL vendor')
add(B,'Shares outstanding on cover page are understated','High','Cover page, shares outstanding line',
 'The cover states 79,350,000 shares outstanding as of November 1, 2024. The Company (transmittal e-mail and Filing Metadata B18), the balance sheet, Note 9 and Note 11 all show 79,450,000 shares, and no share activity after September 30 has been identified.',
 'Form 10-Q cover page (number of shares outstanding of each class of common stock as of the latest practicable date); dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding tag (Regulation S-T Rule 406).',
 'Revise to 79,450,000. Have the transfer agent confirm the count as of the latest practicable date shortly before filing, and update the date if it is changed.','Company (Legal) / transfer agent')
add(B,'Cover page check boxes are not completed','High','Cover page, Section 13/15(d) reporting, Interactive Data, filer status and shell company boxes',
 'The draft shows \"Yes No\" with neither box selected for (i) the reports-filed-in-preceding-12-months question, (ii) the Interactive Data File question and (iii) the shell company question. None of the filer-status boxes is checked; \"Large accelerated filer\" is bolded but unmarked. The EGC transition-period box should be left blank (not an EGC). The Q2 2024 10-Q cover shows the correct completion.',
 'Form 10-Q cover page; Exchange Act Rule 12b-2 (filer status definitions); Regulation S-T Rule 405.',
 'Mark: reports filed - Yes [X]; Interactive Data - Yes [X]; Large accelerated filer [X] (all other filer-status boxes unchecked); EGC election box blank; shell company - No [X]. If the late-filing scenario in Finding 1 arose, re-evaluate the answer to the first question in future reports.','Hargrove')
add(B,'Commission File Number inconsistent with prior filing','High','Cover page',
 'The draft shows Commission File Number 001-35487. The filed Q2 2024 Form 10-Q excerpt shows 001-34762. Only one can be correct, and the number must match the Company EDGAR record (CIK 0001587342).',
 'Form 10-Q cover page; dei:EntityFileNumber tag (Regulation S-T Rule 406).',
 'Verify the Exchange Act file number against EDGAR and prior 10-K/10-Q filings and conform the cover (and the XBRL dei tag).','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')
add(B,'Table of contents omits the statements of comprehensive income; page references unreliable','Low','Table of Contents',
 'The TOC lists no Statements of Comprehensive Income (see Finding 8). The page references (e.g., Statements of Changes in Stockholders Equity at page 6 followed by Cash Flows at page 10) were drafted before the content was final.',
 'General presentation; Form 10-Q General Instruction C (item captions).',
 'Add the comprehensive income statement to the TOC and update all page references after the content is finalized. Hyperlink TOC entries in the EDGAR version.','Hargrove / financial printer')

C='C. Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Part I, Item 1)'
add(C,'Prior-year cash flow column missing - placeholder \"[TO BE ADDED]\"','Critical','Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows',
 'The nine months ended September 30, 2023 column is blank throughout and carries a \"[TO BE ADDED]\" placeholder. All supplemental cash flow disclosures for 2023 are also blank.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(c)(3) (statements of cash flows for the year-to-date period and the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal year); ASC 230.',
 'Insert the full comparative nine months 2023 cash flow statement and supplemental disclosures, tied to the Q3 2023 Form 10-Q (as recast, if applicable). Ridgeline to complete its review procedures on the comparative column.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(C,'Balance sheet comparative column mislabeled \"December 31, 2024\"','Critical','Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets (both asset and liability/equity pages)',
 'The comparative column is headed \"December 31, 2024\", a date that has not yet occurred. It should read December 31, 2023 (the audited fiscal year-end balance sheet, as stated in the prefatory note). The equity caption itself refers to \"December 31, 2023\".',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(c)(1) (balance sheet as of the end of the most recent fiscal quarter and the end of the preceding fiscal year).',
 'Change both column headings to \"December 31, 2023\" and confirm the XBRL context dates.','Company (Finance)')
add(C,'Statements of comprehensive income omitted','High','Part I, Item 1 (financial statements); TOC',
 'The Company has other comprehensive income items: foreign currency translation, cash flow hedges and pension, with OCI of $(4.3) million in Q3 2024 and $(6.4) million for the nine months. No statement of comprehensive income, and no single continuous statement of operations and comprehensive income, is presented. The XBRL exhibit description in the Checklist also omits it.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(c)(2) and Rule 10-01(a)(... ) as applied to comprehensive income; ASC 220-10-45-1, 45-1A/1B and 45-18 (total comprehensive income required in interim financial statements). Reclassification-out-of-AOCI disclosures under ASC 220-10-45-17 also apply.',
 'Add a Condensed Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2024 and 2023 (net income, each OCI component net of tax, total comprehensive income). Add AOCI reclassification disclosure to Note 11. Update the TOC and the Exhibit 101 description.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(C,'Nine-month 2024 stockholders equity roll-forward does not tie to the balance sheet or to the Q3 roll-forward','Critical','Statements of Changes in Stockholders Equity - Nine Months Ended September 30, 2024',
 'The nine-month statement ends at APIC $1,133.5 million, retained earnings $1,435.6 million and total equity $2,525.2 million. The balance sheet and the three-month roll-forward show $1,128.5 million, $1,402.7 million and $2,487.3 million at the same date: differences of $5.0 million (APIC), $32.9 million (retained earnings) and $37.9 million (total). The implied first-half activity is also inconsistent. Starting from January 1, 2024 balances, the July 1, 2024 opening balances imply first-half dividends of about $58.3 million and APIC activity $5.0 million lower than the nine-month column shows. Tax withholding on share-based compensation is shown as $(0.3) million in equity but $(3.5) million in financing cash flows.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(7) (analysis of changes in each caption of stockholders equity for the current and comparative quarter and year-to-date periods); Regulation S-X Rule 3-04.',
 'Finance and Ridgeline to reconcile the quarterly and year-to-date roll-forwards to the general ledger and the balance sheet. Correct dividends declared, APIC activity and the tax-withholding line, and confirm that the three-month and nine-month statements end at identical balances.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(C,'Q3 2024 dividend declared September 28, 2024 not reflected; dividends per share not disclosed','High','Statements of Changes in Stockholders Equity (three and nine months); balance sheet; Note 11; Note 13',
 'The Board declared a $0.16 per share dividend (about $12.7 million) on September 28, 2024, payable October 25, 2024. The three-month roll-forward shows no dividends declared. The nine-month \"dividends declared\" ($25.4 million) equals dividends paid in the cash flow statement, which implies the September 28 declaration was not accrued. The dividend should be a liability (dividends payable within accrued liabilities) and a reduction of retained earnings at September 30, 2024. Per-share dividend amounts are not presented for any period. The comparable Q3 2023 three-month roll-forward also shows no dividend; confirm whether this is correct.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(7) and Rule 3-04 (dividends per share for each class of shares must be stated in the analysis of changes in equity); U.S. GAAP (a cash dividend is recognized as a liability and a charge to retained earnings on the declaration date); Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant events).',
 'Record the $12.7 million declaration in Q3 2024 (retained earnings and accrued liabilities/dividends payable). Present dividends declared per share ($0.16 per quarter) in each roll-forward. Add a dividend paragraph to Note 11, and conform MD&A liquidity and the non-cash financing disclosure (dividends declared but unpaid).','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(C,'Diluted EPS for nine months ended September 30, 2023 inconsistent ($1.53 vs. $1.54)','High','Statement of Operations (EPS table); Note 9; MD&A nine-month discussion',
 'Net income of $122.8 million divided by 79.8 million diluted weighted shares is $1.539, which rounds to $1.54. Note 9 shows $1.54. The face of the statement of operations and MD&A show $1.53.',
 'ASC 260-10-45-2 and 45-7 (EPS presentation on the face of the income statement); internal consistency of the filing (Rule 12b-20 under the Exchange Act).',
 'Confirm the as-filed Q3 2023 amount. If $1.54 is correct, conform the face of the statement and MD&A. If a different share count was used, correct Note 9. Present weighted-average shares at consistent precision (the face shows 80.15/80.05 to two decimals and the other periods to one).','Company (Finance)')
add(C,'December 31, 2023 debt on balance sheet does not agree to debt footnote','High','Balance sheet (Long-term debt, net of current portion, $745.0 million); Note 5 debt table ($697.5 million)',
 'Note 5 shows total debt of $772.5 million (term loan $672.5 million, notes $100.0 million) and long-term debt of $697.5 million at December 31, 2023. The balance sheet shows long-term debt of $745.0 million, which with the $75.0 million current portion implies total debt of $820.0 million. The difference is $47.5 million. Note 5 is consistent with the $37.5 million term-loan repayment in the cash flow statement ($672.5 - $37.5 = $635.0), so the balance sheet comparative appears misstated. That would also mean the December 31, 2023 liability totals foot only because of the wrong amount.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(c)(1) and Rule 5-02; the December 31, 2023 balance sheet must agree to the audited balance sheet in the FY2023 Form 10-K.',
 'Agree the December 31, 2023 column to the audited FY2023 balance sheet and correct either the balance sheet or Note 5. Re-foot total liabilities and total liabilities and equity.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(C,'Cash flow statement presentation items','Medium','Statements of Cash Flows',
 '(i) The caption refers to \"cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash\", but the balance sheet shows only cash and cash equivalents and no restricted-cash reconciliation is given. (ii) The line \"Repayments of revolving credit facility (0.0)\" should be removed or completed. (iii) Tax withholding of $(3.5) million does not agree to the equity statement ($(0.3) million) (see Finding 9). (iv) The dividend declared but unpaid at September 30, 2024 should be disclosed as a non-cash financing activity.',
 'ASC 230-10-45 and 230-10-50-8 (reconciliation of restricted cash to the balance sheet); ASC 230-10-50-3 (non-cash investing and financing activities).',
 'Remove the restricted-cash references if none exist, or add the reconciliation. Delete the zero line. Reconcile the withholding amount. Add dividends declared but unpaid ($12.7 million) to the supplemental non-cash disclosure.','Company (Finance)')

D='D. Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements'
add(D,'Note 3 (PolyShield) omits required ASC 805 disclosures','High','Note 3 - Business Combinations',
 'Note 3 gives the consideration and a condensed preliminary allocation only. It omits: (a) the contingent consideration arrangement - the basis for determining payment (revenue targets over 24 months), the range of undiscounted outcomes or maximum payable, and whether the $25.0 million is fair value or the face amount (Note 12 calls it acquisition-date fair value of $25.0 million, which equals the headline earnout); (b) intangible assets by major class ($42.6 million) with weighted-average amortization periods; (c) qualitative description of factors making up goodwill and the amount of tax-deductible goodwill; (d) goodwill assigned by segment (Advanced Materials); (e) acquisition-related costs and the income statement line in which they were recognized (MD&A cites PolyShield costs in SG&A, and the integration consulting engagement with Apex Strategic Advisors is fixed at $3.8 million); (f) revenue and earnings of PolyShield since July 15, 2024 (MD&A discloses about $8.6 million of revenue but the note does not); (g) supplemental pro forma revenue and earnings as if the acquisition had occurred on January 1, 2023, for the three- and nine-month periods; (h) fair value, gross contractual amount and expected uncollectible amount of acquired receivables ($18.7 million); and (i) the specific items for which the initial accounting is incomplete and the reasons. The cash-flow amount (\$136.8 million net of $3.2 million cash acquired) agrees to the $140.0 million cash consideration.',
 'ASC 805-10-50-2 (including (h) pro forma and acquiree revenue and earnings for public business entities) and 805-10-50-6; ASC 805-20-50-1 (receivables, contingencies); ASC 805-30-50-1 (goodwill factors, tax-deductible goodwill, by segment) and 805-30-50-4 (contingent consideration); ASC 350-30-50-1; ASC 270-10-50-7; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant events since year-end). The client specifically asked for a complete ASC 805 interim disclosure.',
 'Expand Note 3 to cover items (a)-(i). Reconcile the $42.6 million intangible allocation to the gross additions in Note 6 (see Finding 16). Cross-reference the Level 3 roll-forward of contingent consideration in Note 12. Disclose any measurement-period adjustments recorded during Q3.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Note 6 intangible asset reconciliation errors','High','Note 6 - Goodwill and Intangible Assets; balance sheet',
 '(i) Note 6 states that finite-lived intangibles plus $41.0 million of indefinite-lived trade names equal the balance-sheet totals at both dates. At December 31, 2023 the result is $443.8 + $41.0 = $484.8 million, not the $543.8 million on the balance sheet (difference $59.0 million). At September 30, 2024, $477.2 + $41.0 = $518.2 million agrees. (ii) Gross carrying amounts rose $66.6 million (customer relationships +$38.3 million, technology +$26.7 million, other +$1.6 million), but the PolyShield allocation assigns only $42.6 million to intangibles. (iii) Accumulated amortization rose $33.2 million, but nine-month amortization expense is stated as $25.6 million. (iv) The balance sheet shows intangibles falling from $543.8 million to $518.2 million despite a $42.6 million acquisition and $25.6 million of amortization. The arithmetic implies about $560.8 million, or $501.8 million using the Note 6 base.',
 'ASC 350-30-50-1 and 50-2; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5); internal consistency (Exchange Act Rule 12b-20).',
 'Finance and Ridgeline to reconcile the intangible roll-forward (opening balance, PolyShield additions by class, amortization, FX) to the general ledger and balance sheet, and to correct Note 6, Note 3 and the balance sheet as needed. Update the impairment statement to cover the nine-month period and the class-action and market-capitalization considerations.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Note 5 debt maturity schedule inconsistent with term loan maturity and amortization','Medium','Note 5 - Debt',
 'Note 5 states that the August 20, 2024 amendment extended the maturity from March 15, 2027 to August 20, 2029 but \"did not modify the term loan facility\". If the term loan still matures on March 15, 2027, the maturity table should show a 2027 balloon payment (about $500+ million) rather than $75.0 million, and \"thereafter\" would fall accordingly. Separately, the schedule implies $18.75 million per quarter (remainder of 2024 $25.0 million; $75.0 million per year), while actual 2024 repayments were $37.5 million for nine months ($12.5 million per quarter). The note also does not say whether the 2029 maturity applies to the term loan. The amendment number is unclear: \"Amendment No. 3\" in the transmittal e-mail and \"Amendment No. 1\" in the Material Contracts Log.',
 'ASC 470-10-50-1 (maturities); Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant changes in long-term debt); Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(1) (liquidity, known trends and commitments).',
 'Confirm the term loan maturity and amortization schedule against the Credit Agreement as amended. Correct the maturity table and describe which tranches the amendment extended. Use the correct amendment number consistently in Note 5, MD&A and the exhibit index.','Company (Treasury/Legal) / Hargrove')
add(D,'Loss contingency disclosure for securities class action is incomplete','High','Note 7 - Commitments and Contingencies; Part II, Item 1',
 'Note 7 describes the complaint but does not give the ASC 450 assessment. It does not say whether a loss is probable, reasonably possible or remote, does not give an estimate of possible loss or range of loss (or state that an estimate cannot be made), and does not say whether any amount has been accrued. It also omits the class period and the named plaintiff. The \"without merit\" statement does not replace the required assessment.',
 'ASC 450-20-50-3 through 50-5 (disclosure where loss is reasonably possible, including an estimate or a statement that an estimate cannot be made); ASC 450-20-25-2; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (material contingencies arising since year-end).',
 'Add a statement such as: \"The litigation is at an early stage; the Company has not recorded an accrual because a loss is not probable and reasonably estimable, and the Company is unable at this time to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss, if any\", subject to Ridgeline and litigation counsel concurrence. Add the class period and lead-plaintiff information. Disclose any D&O insurance and retention only if appropriate. This preserves the litigation position while meeting the disclosure requirement.','Company (Legal) / litigation counsel / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Segment note presents only three-month data; reconciliation incomplete','High','Note 8 - Segment Information',
 'Segment revenue and operating income are given only for the three-month periods. No nine-month (year-to-date) segment information is presented. MD&A concedes this (\"our segment footnote presents quarterly segment results\"). The reconciliation stops at consolidated operating income rather than income before income taxes. No disclosure is given of the material change in Advanced Materials segment assets from the PolyShield acquisition.',
 'ASC 280-10-50-32 (interim disclosure of segment revenues and profit or loss for the current quarter and year-to-date, material changes in segment assets, and a reconciliation of total segment profit or loss to consolidated income before income taxes); ASC 280-10-50-33.',
 'Add nine-month 2024 and 2023 segment revenue and operating income. Extend the reconciliation to income before income taxes (interest expense and other income (expense), net). Disclose Advanced Materials segment assets or the material change in them. Ensure the ASU 2023-07 annual disclosures are planned for the FY2024 Form 10-K.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Fair value note lacks Level 3 roll-forward and quantitative unobservable inputs; derivative presentation unclear','Medium','Note 12 - Fair Value Measurements',
 'The contingent consideration (Level 3) moved from $25.0 million to $24.8 million, but no roll-forward is given showing the change recognized in earnings and the line item affected. No range or weighted average of the significant unobservable inputs (revenue projections, volatility, discount rate) is given. The table does not say whether the interest rate swaps ($3.1 million) and FX forwards ($1.8 million) are assets or liabilities or where they appear on the balance sheet, which matters because AOCI shows cumulative hedge losses of $9.8 million.',
 'ASC 820-10-50-2(c)(2) and 50-2(bbb) (Level 3 reconciliation and quantitative information, required in interim periods for public entities); ASC 815-10-50-4A to 4C; ASC 270-10-50-1.',
 'Add a Level 3 roll-forward and a table of quantitative unobservable inputs. Split the derivatives into assets and liabilities, give their balance sheet captions, and add the cash flow hedge reclassification information.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Recently issued accounting pronouncements disclosure is boilerplate','Low','Note 2 - Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements',
 'ASU 2023-07 applies to the Company FY2024 Form 10-K (annual periods beginning after December 15, 2023) and will apply retrospectively to all prior periods presented. With one quarter left, \"currently evaluating\" is unlikely to satisfy staff expectations. ASU 2023-09 disclosure is also generic. Also consider the ASU 2024-03 (expense disaggregation) project if the FASB has issued it by the filing date.',
 'SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 11.M (SAB 74) - disclose the expected effect of adopting standards issued but not yet effective, to the extent reasonably estimable.',
 'State that the Company will adopt ASU 2023-07 in its FY2024 Form 10-K on a retrospective basis, describe the expected incremental disclosures (significant segment expenses provided to the CODM, CODM title and position), and confirm the Company does not expect an effect on financial position or results.','Company (Finance)')
add(D,'Subsequent events note','Low','Note 13 - Subsequent Events',
 'The note states that no subsequent events require disclosure. Before filing, confirm that nothing has occurred since September 30, 2024. Examples to check: the October 25, 2024 dividend payment (declared pre-quarter-end; see Finding 10), developments in the class action (e.g., lead plaintiff appointment, related derivative suits), any further revolver draws or repayments, and any measurement-period adjustments.',
 'ASC 855-10-25 and 50; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5).',
 'Have management perform an updated subsequent-events review through the filing date and coordinate with Ridgeline cut-off procedures.','Company (Finance/Legal)')

E='E. Management Discussion and Analysis (Part I, Item 2)'
add(E,'MD&A omits known trends and uncertainties from the securities class action and the earnout obligation','Medium','MD&A - Overview; Liquidity and Capital Resources; Critical Accounting Estimates',
 'MD&A does not discuss the September 5, 2024 class action, which alleges misstatements about Specialty Coatings revenue recognition (the Company largest segment), as a known uncertainty. It also omits the $25.0 million contingent consideration payable over 24 months, covenant compliance and headroom (4.0x maximum net leverage; 3.0x minimum interest coverage), and the remaining $82.5 million share repurchase capacity. The critical accounting estimates discussion is qualitative only for the business combination and the contingent consideration.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(1) (material cash requirements, known trends, commitments), 303(b)(2)(ii) (known trends or uncertainties reasonably likely to have a material impact), 303(b)(3) (critical accounting estimates - qualitative and quantitative), and 303(c) (interim period requirements); SEC Release No. 33-10890 (2020 MD&A amendments).',
 'Add a short litigation cross-reference in the Overview or liquidity discussion that is consistent with Note 7 and avoids characterizing the merits beyond what Note 7 says. Add the earnout payment profile and covenant compliance to the liquidity discussion. Give sensitivity or range information for the contingent consideration and intangible valuation estimates.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')
add(E,'\"Net debt\" presented without non-GAAP compliance','Medium','MD&A - Liquidity and Capital Resources',
 'MD&A presents \"net debt\" of $472.6 million (total debt less cash). The arithmetic is correct. Net debt is a non-GAAP financial measure, and the draft gives no statement of why it is useful to investors and no formal reconciliation presented with equal or greater prominence to total debt.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 10(e)(1)(i) and Regulation G; SEC staff Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations on Non-GAAP Financial Measures.',
 'Either delete the measure, or add a reconciliation table (total debt, less cash and cash equivalents, equals net debt) and a statement of usefulness and of any other purposes for which management uses it.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')
add(E,'Nine-month and segment MD&A not fully quantified; EPS conformity','Low','MD&A - Nine Months Results; Segment Results Discussion',
 'The nine-month segment discussion is qualitative only, with no nine-month segment revenue or operating income figures (consistent with the gap in Note 8). SG&A and the inventory step-up effect from the PolyShield acquisition are not quantified, although they are cited as drivers. Nine-month 2023 diluted EPS should be conformed (Finding 11). The organic versus acquired split for Advanced Materials (about $8.6 million from PolyShield out of $13.1 million) should also appear in the segment section, and PolyShield operating income contribution should be quantified if material.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(2) and 303(c)(2) (discussion of material changes in results for the year-to-date and quarterly periods, including quantification of offsetting factors where practicable).',
 'Add nine-month segment figures and quantify the acquisition-related cost and step-up effects. Conform EPS.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')

F_='F. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk (Part I, Item 3)'
add(F_,'Interest rate sensitivity figure does not reconcile to variable-rate debt','Low','Part I, Item 3 - Interest Rate Risk',
 'Variable-rate borrowings are $685.0 million ($635.0 million term loan plus $50.0 million revolver), so a 100 basis-point increase implies about $6.85 million of annual interest. The draft states $6.4 million. This may reflect swap hedging, but the hedged notional is not disclosed. The lead-in states there have been no material changes \"except as discussed below\", but the section does not identify what changed (e.g., the higher revolver commitment and the $50.0 million draw).',
 'Regulation S-K Item 305(c) (quarterly disclosure of material changes in market risk); Item 305(a).',

A Rule 12b-25 notification (Form 12b-25 due by November 13, 2024; 10-Q then due by Monday, November 18, 2024) is available only if the delay could not be eliminated without unreasonable effort or expense, which a scheduling preference does not satisfy.',
 'Reset the target filing date to no later than Tuesday, November 12, 2024. We recommend targeting Friday, November 8, 2024, with November 12 kept as the fallback.  'Company (Legal/Finance); XBRL vendor; Hargrove')

(iii) Tax withholding of $(3.5) million does not agree to the equity statement ($(0.3) million) (see Finding 9). (iv) The dividend declared but unpaid at September 30, 2024 should be disclosed as a non-cash financing activity.',
 'ASC 230-10-45 and 230-10-50-8 (reconciliation of restricted cash to the balance sheet); ASC 230-10-50-3 (non-cash investing and financing activities).',
 'Remove the restricted-cash references if none exist, or add the reconciliation. Delete the zero line. Reconcile the withholding amount. Add dividends declared but unpaid ($12.7 million) to the supplemental non-cash disclosure.','Company (Finance)')

D='D. Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements'
add(D,'Note 3 (PolyShield) omits required ASC 805 disclosures','High','Note 3 - Business Combinations',
 'Note 3 gives the consideration and a condensed preliminary allocation only. It omits: (a) the contingent consideration arrangement - the basis for determining payment (revenue targets over 24 months), the range of undiscounted outcomes or maximum payable, and whether the $25.0 million is fair value or the face amount (Note 12 calls it acquisition-date fair value of $25.0 million, which equals the headline earnout); (b) intangible assets by major class ($42.6 million) with weighted-average amortization periods; (c) qualitative description of factors making up goodwill and the amount of tax-deductible goodwill; (d) goodwill assigned by segment (Advanced Materials); (e) acquisition-related costs and the income statement line in which they were recognized (MD&A cites PolyShield costs in SG&A, and the integration consulting engagement with Apex Strategic Advisors is fixed at $3.8 million); (f) revenue and earnings of PolyShield since July 15, 2024 (MD&A discloses about $8.6 million of revenue but the note does not); (g) supplemental pro forma revenue and earnings as if the acquisition had occurred on January 1, 2023, for the three- and nine-month periods; (h) fair value, gross contractual amount and expected uncollectible amount of acquired receivables ($18.7 million); and (i) the specific items for which the initial accounting is incomplete and the reasons. The cash-flow amount (\$136.8 million net of $3.2 million cash acquired) agrees to the $140.0 million cash consideration.',
 'ASC 805-10-50-2 (including (h) pro forma and acquiree revenue and earnings for public business entities) and 805-10-50-6; ASC 805-20-50-1 (receivables, contingencies); ASC 805-30-50-1 (goodwill factors, tax-deductible goodwill, by segment) and 805-30-50-4 (contingent consideration); ASC 350-30-50-1; ASC 270-10-50-7; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant events since year-end). The client specifically asked for a complete ASC 805 interim disclosure.',
 'Expand Note 3 to cover items (a)-(i). Reconcile the $42.6 million intangible allocation to the gross additions in Note 6 (see Finding 16). Cross-reference the Level 3 roll-forward of contingent consideration in Note 12. Disclose any measurement-period adjustments recorded during Q3.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Note 6 intangible asset reconciliation errors','High','Note 6 - Goodwill and Intangible Assets; balance sheet',
 '(i) Note 6 states that finite-lived intangibles plus $41.0 million of indefinite-lived trade names equal the balance-sheet totals at both dates. At December 31, 2023 the result is $443.8 + $41.0 = $484.8 million, not the $543.8 million on the balance sheet (difference $59.0 million). At September 30, 2024, $477.2 + $41.0 = $518.2 million agrees. (ii) Gross carrying amounts rose $66.6 million (customer relationships +$38.3 million, technology +$26.7 million, other +$1.6 million), but the PolyShield allocation assigns only $42.6 million to intangibles. (iii) Accumulated amortization rose $33.2 million, but nine-month amortization expense is stated as $25.6 million. (iv) The balance sheet shows intangibles falling from $543.8 million to $518.2 million despite a $42.6 million acquisition and $25.6 million of amortization. The arithmetic implies about $560.8 million, or $501.8 million using the Note 6 base.',
 'ASC 350-30-50-1 and 50-2; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5); internal consistency (Exchange Act Rule 12b-20).',
 'Finance and Ridgeline to reconcile the intangible roll-forward (opening balance, PolyShield additions by class, amortization, FX) to the general ledger and balance sheet, and to correct Note 6, Note 3 and the balance sheet as needed. Update the impairment statement to cover the nine-month period and the class-action and market-capitalization considerations.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Note 5 debt maturity schedule inconsistent with term loan maturity and amortization','Medium','Note 5 - Debt',
 'Note 5 states that the August 20, 2024 amendment extended the maturity from March 15, 2027 to August 20, 2029 but \"did not modify the term loan facility\". If the term loan still matures on March 15, 2027, the maturity table should show a 2027 balloon payment (about $500+ million) rather than $75.0 million, and \"thereafter\" would fall accordingly. Separately, the schedule implies $18.75 million per quarter (remainder of 2024 $25.0 million; $75.0 million per year), while actual 2024 repayments were $37.5 million for nine months ($12.5 million per quarter). The note also does not say whether the 2029 maturity applies to the term loan. The amendment number is unclear: \"Amendment No. 3\" in the transmittal e-mail and \"Amendment No. 1\" in the Material Contracts Log.',
 'ASC 470-10-50-1 (maturities); Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant changes in long-term debt); Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(1) (liquidity, known trends and commitments).',
 'Confirm the term loan maturity and amortization schedule against the Credit Agreement as amended. Correct the maturity table and describe which tranches the amendment extended. Use the correct amendment number consistently in Note 5, MD&A and the exhibit index.','Company (Treasury/Legal) / Hargrove')
add(D,'Loss contingency disclosure for securities class action is incomplete','High','Note 7 - Commitments and Contingencies; Part II, Item 1',
 'Note 7 describes the complaint but does not give the ASC 450 assessment. It does not say whether a loss is probable, reasonably possible or remote, does not give an estimate of possible loss or range of loss (or state that an estimate cannot be made), and does not say whether any amount has been accrued. It also omits the class period and the named plaintiff. The \"without merit\" statement does not replace the required assessment.',
 'ASC 450-20-50-3 through 50-5 (disclosure where loss is reasonably possible, including an estimate or a statement that an estimate cannot be made); ASC 450-20-25-2; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (material contingencies arising since year-end).',
 'Add a statement such as: \"The litigation is at an early stage; the Company has not recorded an accrual because a loss is not probable and reasonably estimable, and the Company is unable at this time to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss, if any\", subject to Ridgeline and litigation counsel concurrence. Add the class period and lead-plaintiff information. Disclose any D&O insurance and retention only if appropriate. This preserves the litigation position while meeting the disclosure requirement.','Company (Legal) / litigation counsel / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Segment note presents only three-month data; reconciliation incomplete','High','Note 8 - Segment Information',
 'Segment revenue and operating income are given only for the three-month periods. No nine-month (year-to-date) segment information is presented. MD&A concedes this (\"our segment footnote presents quarterly segment results\"). The reconciliation stops at consolidated operating income rather than income before income taxes. No disclosure is given of the material change in Advanced Materials segment assets from the PolyShield acquisition.',
 'ASC 280-10-50-32 (interim disclosure of segment revenues and profit or loss for the current quarter and year-to-date, material changes in segment assets, and a reconciliation of total segment profit or loss to consolidated income before income taxes); ASC 280-10-50-33.',
 'Add nine-month 2024 and 2023 segment revenue and operating income. Extend the reconciliation to income before income taxes (interest expense and other income (expense), net). Disclose Advanced Materials segment assets or the material change in them. Ensure the ASU 2023-07 annual disclosures are planned for the FY2024 Form 10-K.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Fair value note lacks Level 3 roll-forward and quantitative unobservable inputs; derivative presentation unclear','Medium','Note 12 - Fair Value Measurements',
 'The contingent consideration (Level 3) moved from $25.0 million to $24.8 million, but no roll-forward is given showing the change recognized in earnings and the line item affected. No range or weighted average of the significant unobservable inputs (revenue projections, volatility, discount rate) is given. The table does not say whether the interest rate swaps ($3.1 million) and FX forwards ($1.8 million) are assets or liabilities or where they appear on the balance sheet, which matters because AOCI shows cumulative hedge losses of $9.8 million.',
 'ASC 820-10-50-2(c)(2) and 50-2(bbb) (Level 3 reconciliation and quantitative information, required in interim periods for public entities); ASC 815-10-50-4A to 4C; ASC 270-10-50-1.',
 'Add a Level 3 roll-forward and a table of quantitative unobservable inputs. Split the derivatives into assets and liabilities, give their balance sheet captions, and add the cash flow hedge reclassification information.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')
add(D,'Recently issued accounting pronouncements disclosure is boilerplate','Low','Note 2 - Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements',
 'ASU 2023-07 applies to the Company FY2024 Form 10-K (annual periods beginning after December 15, 2023) and will apply retrospectively to all prior periods presented. With one quarter left, \"currently evaluating\" is unlikely to satisfy staff expectations. ASU 2023-09 disclosure is also generic. Also consider the ASU 2024-03 (expense disaggregation) project if the FASB has issued it by the filing date.',
 'SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 11.M (SAB 74) - disclose the expected effect of adopting standards issued but not yet effective, to the extent reasonably estimable.',
 'State that the Company will adopt ASU 2023-07 in its FY2024 Form 10-K on a retrospective basis, describe the expected incremental disclosures (significant segment expenses provided to the CODM, CODM title and position), and confirm the Company does not expect an effect on financial position or results.','Company (Finance)')
add(D,'Subsequent events note','Low','Note 13 - Subsequent Events',
 'The note states that no subsequent events require disclosure. Before filing, confirm that nothing has occurred since September 30, 2024. Examples to check: the October 25, 2024 dividend payment (declared pre-quarter-end; see Finding 10), developments in the class action (e.g., lead plaintiff appointment, related derivative suits), any further revolver draws or repayments, and any measurement-period adjustments.',
 'ASC 855-10-25 and 50; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5).',
 'Have management perform an updated subsequent-events review through the filing date and coordinate with Ridgeline cut-off procedures.','Company (Finance/Legal)')

E='E. Management Discussion and Analysis (Part I, Item 2)'
add(E,'MD&A omits known trends and uncertainties from the securities class action and the earnout obligation','Medium','MD&A - Overview; Liquidity and Capital Resources; Critical Accounting Estimates',
 'MD&A does not discuss the September 5, 2024 class action, which alleges misstatements about Specialty Coatings revenue recognition (the Company largest segment), as a known uncertainty. It also omits the $25.0 million contingent consideration payable over 24 months, covenant compliance and headroom (4.0x maximum net leverage; 3.0x minimum interest coverage), and the remaining $82.5 million share repurchase capacity. The critical accounting estimates discussion is qualitative only for the business combination and the contingent consideration.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(1) (material cash requirements, known trends, commitments), 303(b)(2)(ii) (known trends or uncertainties reasonably likely to have a material impact), 303(b)(3) (critical accounting estimates - qualitative and quantitative), and 303(c) (interim period requirements); SEC Release No. 33-10890 (2020 MD&A amendments).',
 'Add a short litigation cross-reference in the Overview or liquidity discussion that is consistent with Note 7 and avoids characterizing the merits beyond what Note 7 says. Add the earnout payment profile and covenant compliance to the liquidity discussion. Give sensitivity or range information for the contingent consideration and intangible valuation estimates.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')
add(E,'\"Net debt\" presented without non-GAAP compliance','Medium','MD&A - Liquidity and Capital Resources',
 'MD&A presents \"net debt\" of $472.6 million (total debt less cash). The arithmetic is correct. Net debt is a non-GAAP financial measure, and the draft gives no statement of why it is useful to investors and no formal reconciliation presented with equal or greater prominence to total debt.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 10(e)(1)(i) and Regulation G; SEC staff Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations on Non-GAAP Financial Measures.',
 'Either delete the measure, or add a reconciliation table (total debt, less cash and cash equivalents, equals net debt) and a statement of usefulness and of any other purposes for which management uses it.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')
add(E,'Nine-month and segment MD&A not fully quantified; EPS conformity','Low','MD&A - Nine Months Results; Segment Results Discussion',
 'The nine-month segment discussion is qualitative only, with no nine-month segment revenue or operating income figures (consistent with the gap in Note 8). SG&A and the inventory step-up effect from the PolyShield acquisition are not quantified, although they are cited as drivers. Nine-month 2023 diluted EPS should be conformed (Finding 11). The organic versus acquired split for Advanced Materials (about $8.6 million from PolyShield out of $13.1 million) should also appear in the segment section, and PolyShield operating income contribution should be quantified if material.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(2) and 303(c)(2) (discussion of material changes in results for the year-to-date and quarterly periods, including quantification of offsetting factors where practicable).',
 'Add nine-month segment figures and quantify the acquisition-related cost and step-up effects. Conform EPS.','Hargrove / Company (Finance)')

F_='F. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk (Part I, Item 3)'
add(F_,'Interest rate sensitivity figure does not reconcile to variable-rate debt','Low','Part I, Item 3 - Interest Rate Risk',
 'Variable-rate borrowings are $685.0 million ($635.0 million term loan plus $50.0 million revolver), so a 100 basis-point increase implies about $6.85 million of annual interest. The draft states $6.4 million. This may reflect swap hedging, but the hedged notional is not disclosed. The lead-in states there have been no material changes \"except as discussed below\", but the section does not identify what changed (e.g., the higher revolver commitment and the $50.0 million draw).',
 'Regulation S-K Item 305(c) (quarterly disclosure of material changes in market risk); Item 305(a).',
 'Reconcile the $6.4 million figure, disclose the swap notional used, and clarify which changes since the FY2023 Form 10-K are being described.','Company (Treasury) / Hargrove')

G='G. Controls and Procedures (Part I, Item 4)'
add(G,'Disclosure controls conclusion missing - placeholder \"[Conclusion to be inserted]\"','Critical','Part I, Item 4 - Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures',
 'The draft describes the evaluation but gives no conclusion. The CEO and CFO must state their conclusion on effectiveness as of September 30, 2024. Paragraph 4(c) of each Section 302 certification certifies that the conclusion is \"presented in this report\", so without it the certifications would be inaccurate. In reaching the conclusion, management should consider the class action allegations about Specialty Coatings revenue recognition and the integration of PolyShield.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 307; Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(b) and 15d-15(b); Item 601(b)(31)(i), paragraph 4(c).',
 'Insert the conclusion, following the Q2 2024 formulation if supported: \"Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of September 30, 2024, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.\" Document the disclosure committee and sub-certification support. If any deficiency is identified, consult us before finalizing.','Company (CEO/CFO/Disclosure Committee) / Hargrove')
add(G,'Changes in ICFR paragraph is internally inconsistent regarding PolyShield','Medium','Part I, Item 4 - Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting',
 'The draft first states there were \"no changes\" in ICFR during the quarter that materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR. It then states that the Company is integrating PolyShield internal controls, with completion expected in the first half of 2025. The draft does not say whether PolyShield will be excluded from management annual ICFR assessment for FY2024, which the SEC staff permits for an acquired business in the year of acquisition.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 308(c); Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(d) and 15d-15(d); SEC staff FAQ on Management Report on ICFR (Question 3) (exclusion of acquired businesses for up to one year).',
 'Revise to: \"On July 15, 2024, we acquired PolyShield... We are in the process of integrating PolyShield into our internal control over financial reporting. Except for the inclusion of PolyShield controls, there were no changes...\" State that management expects to exclude PolyShield from its December 31, 2024 ICFR assessment, if that is the plan.','Company (Finance) / Hargrove')

H='H. Part II - Other Information'
add(H,'Legal Proceedings disclosure lacks Item 103 elements','Medium','Part II, Item 1 - Legal Proceedings',
 'The disclosure names the court, date, case number, defendants and claims. It omits the name of the plaintiff (the principal party bringing the action) and the alleged class period, and its description of the factual basis is thin. It repeats Note 7 instead of cross-referencing it.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 103(a) (name of court, date instituted, principal parties, description of the factual basis alleged and relief sought; cross-reference to the financial statement notes permitted); Form 10-Q Part II, Item 1.',
 'Add the named plaintiff and class period. Consider cross-referencing Note 7 to avoid inconsistency. Keep the \"intends to vigorously defend\" language, but do not characterize the merits further. Have litigation counsel review the language for consistency with pleadings.','Hargrove / litigation counsel')
add(H,'Issuer repurchase table - program details and withheld shares','Low','Part II, Item 2(c)',
 'The table and narrative do not give the date the $150.0 million program was announced. The CFS shows $3.5 million of nine-month tax withholding on equity awards. Shares withheld to cover taxes count as issuer purchases and must be reported in the monthly table for Q3 if any occurred.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 703 and Instructions to Item 703 (date each plan or program was announced, dollar amount approved, expiration date).',
 'Add the announcement date. Confirm with Finance whether any shares were withheld or surrendered in July-September 2024 and, if so, report them in the table with an explanatory footnote.','Company (Legal/Finance) / Hargrove')
add(H,'Risk factors and Other Information','Low','Part II, Items 1A and 5',
 'Item 1A updates for PolyShield integration and the class action are appropriate. Consider whether the expanded revolver/indebtedness and the earnout obligation need updates, and whether the \"macroeconomic\" factor is a material change from the FY2023 Form 10-K or should be deleted. Item 5 Rule 10b5-1 disclosure is properly framed. Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that no director or officer adopted or terminated a plan during the quarter, and that no Form 8-K items (Item 5(a)) went unreported.',
 'Form 10-Q Part II, Item 1A (material changes from previously disclosed risk factors); Regulation S-K Items 105 and 408(a); Form 10-Q Part II, Item 5(a).',
 'Confirm with management and revise as needed.','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')

I='I. Exhibits - Form 10-Q Item 6 Exhibit Index and Exhibit Index Checklist'
add(I,'Credit Agreement amendment of August 20, 2024 not filed as an exhibit','Critical','10-Q Item 6 exhibit index; Checklist (no row); Material Contracts Log row 2 (\"TBD\")',
 'The August 20, 2024 amendment modifies a material contract (Credit Agreement, Checklist Exhibit 10.1). It raised the revolver to $500.0 million and extended maturity to 2029. The Company 8-K of August 22, 2024 described it but did not file the text. The amendment is neither on the 10-Q exhibit index nor on the Checklist.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(a)(4) (a material contract executed or becoming effective during the quarter, and any amendment or modification to a previously filed exhibit, must be filed with the Form 10-Q for that period); Item 601(b)(10)(i); Item 601(a)(5) (schedules may be omitted with a list); Item 601(b)(10)(iv) (redaction of immaterial, competitively harmful information with required legend).',
 'File the amendment as Exhibit 10.1 (\"filed herewith\"). Settle the amendment number (\"No. 1\" vs. \"No. 3\") from the executed document. If it is Amendment No. 3, confirm that Amendments No. 1 and No. 2 were previously filed and list them as incorporated by reference. Apply Item 601(a)(5)/(a)(6)/(b)(10)(iv) redactions and legends as appropriate.','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')
add(I,'PolyShield Equity Purchase Agreement not filed as an exhibit','Critical','10-Q Item 6 exhibit index; Checklist (no row); Material Contracts Log row 3 (\"TBD\")',
 'The July 15, 2024 Equity Purchase Agreement ($165.0 million, marked \"Material\" in the Company own log) was announced on Form 8-K on July 17, 2024 without filing the agreement. It has not been filed and does not appear on either exhibit list.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(2) (material plans of acquisition; the exhibit table applies Item 601(b)(2) to Form 10-Q) and Item 601(a)(4); Item 601(b)(2)(ii) (schedules may be omitted, with a list of omitted schedules and an undertaking to furnish them supplementally); Item 601(a)(6) and (b)(2)(ii) redaction rules.',
 'File as Exhibit 2.1 (\"filed herewith\"), omitting schedules and exhibits under Item 601(a)(5)/(b)(2)(ii) with the required list and undertaking. Apply the redaction legend for any confidential terms. Finalize the \"Exhibit Filing Required?\" column in the Material Contracts Log as \"Yes\" for rows 2-3.','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')
add(I,'Exhibit 104 (Cover Page Interactive Data File) omitted','High','10-Q Item 6 exhibit index; Checklist',
 'Neither the 10-Q exhibit index nor the Checklist lists Exhibit 104. The Company specifically asked us to confirm it.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(104); Regulation S-T Rule 406 (Inline XBRL cover page tagging).',
 'Add: \"104 - Cover Page Interactive Data File (formatted as Inline XBRL and contained in Exhibit 101)\".','Hargrove / XBRL vendor')
add(I,'Exhibit 101 descriptions incomplete or inconsistent','Medium','10-Q Item 6 exhibit index; Checklist row 20',
 'The 10-Q index lists 101.INS through 101.PRE, but the Instance Document entry lacks the standard Inline XBRL legend. The Checklist lists \"101\" as a single item whose description omits the statements of comprehensive income (Finding 8) and lists the statements in a different order from the 10-Q. The Checklist shows the XBRL work \"In Progress\", with delivery on November 12, which is also the legal due date.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(101)(i); Regulation S-T Rules 405 and 406; EDGAR Filer Manual Vol. II, Ch. 6.',
 'Revise 101.INS to read: \"Inline XBRL Instance Document - the instance document does not appear in the Interactive Data File because its XBRL tags are embedded within the Inline XBRL document.\" Conform the Checklist to the six-component presentation, add the comprehensive income statement, and move XBRL delivery forward (Finding 1).','Hargrove / XBRL vendor / Company (Finance)')
add(I,'10-Q exhibit index lacks hyperlinks, filing-status legends and furnished designation','Medium','10-Q Item 6 exhibit index',
 'The draft index lists only Exhibits 31.1-32.2 and 101. It has (i) no \"filed herewith\" or \"furnished herewith\" markers, (ii) no statement that Exhibits 32.1 and 32.2 are furnished and are not deemed \"filed\" for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act, and (iii) for any exhibit incorporated by reference, no hyperlink to the previously filed document. Its descriptions of Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 omit the Rule 15d-14(a) and Section 302 references used in the Checklist.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(a)(2) and Regulation S-T Rule 105 (active hyperlinks to exhibits incorporated by reference); Item 601(b)(32)(ii) (Section 906 certifications furnished and not filed); Exchange Act Rule 13a-14(b).',
 'Rebuild the exhibit index in the form set out in Appendix A to this memo, with hyperlinks, footnotes and legends.','Hargrove')
add(I,'Checklist includes items that are not exhibits or are not required for this 10-Q','Medium','Checklist rows 4-15 (Exhibits 3.1-10.7)',
 '(i) Row 15 lists the Form S-3 shelf registration statement as \"Exhibit 10.7\". A registration statement is not a material contract and is not an Item 601 exhibit. It must not appear in the exhibit index. (ii) Rows 4-14 (charter, bylaws, specimen certificate, indenture, Description of Securities, Credit Agreement and compensatory arrangements) were not amended or entered into during Q3 2024. A Form 10-Q requires only new or amended items, and the Description of Securities (Item 601(b)(4)(vi)) is a Form 10-K exhibit. Including them is allowed, but every such entry then requires an accurate hyperlinked reference. (iii) Numbering would collide with the new Exhibit 10.1 (Finding 30).',
 'Regulation S-K Item 601(a)(4) and the Item 601(a) exhibit table (exhibits required for Form 10-Q); Item 601(b)(3), (b)(4)(vi) and (b)(10)(iii).',
 'Delete row 15. Either drop the unchanged historical exhibits from the 10-Q index (our recommendation, consistent with market practice) or keep them with hyperlinks. Renumber so that new exhibits (2.1, 10.1) take the lead numbers.','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')
add(I,'Checklist source reference errors','Medium','Checklist row 7 (Exhibit 4.2); row 2 header',
 'Exhibit 4.2 (Indenture dated November 10, 2022) is said to be incorporated from a Form 8-K \"filed November 12, 2022\", which was a Saturday, so no EDGAR filing could bear that date. Note 5 also calls the Notes a private placement. Confirm that the Indenture was filed and identify the correct filing date and exhibit number.',
 'Regulation S-K Item 10(d) and Item 601(a)(2) (incorporation by reference must identify the document precisely and include a working hyperlink); Exchange Act Rule 12b-23.',
 'Verify each incorporated-by-reference source (form, filing date, exhibit number, file number) against EDGAR, correct row 7, and generate hyperlinks from the EDGAR URLs.','Company (Legal) / Hargrove')
add(I,'Checklist summary counts and data integrity errors','Low','Checklist summary (rows 23-26); Material Contracts Log',
 '(i) \"Total Exhibits Listed: 18\" - the Checklist lists 17 exhibit rows. (ii) \"Draft Complete: 5\" - only 4 rows (31.1, 31.2, 32.1, 32.2) carry that status. (iii) The Material Contracts Log assigns the Charlotte lease amendment to an \"Industrial Solutions\" segment, but the Company reports only Specialty Coatings and Advanced Materials (Note 1, Note 8). (iv) The Log materiality column for the Credit Agreement describes a \"$1.25B+ credit facility\" (the original $750.0 million term loan plus $500.0 million revolver); the term loan outstanding is now $635.0 million.',
 'Internal controls over the disclosure process (Exchange Act Rule 13a-15(e)).',
 'Correct the counts after revision, fix the segment reference and update the Log.','Company (Legal)')
add(I,'Exhibit 15 / review report - confirm no reference to Ridgeline review','Low','Part I, Item 1; Exhibit index',
 'The review report is not included, which is correct when the filing does not refer to a review. If the Company or Ridgeline later decides to refer to the AS 4105 review in the 10-Q, the review report must be included. Because the 10-Q is incorporated into the effective Form S-3 (and any Form S-8), an awareness letter would then be required as Exhibit 15.',
 'Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(d); Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(15); Securities Act Rule 436(c).',
 'Keep the draft free of any reference to the auditor review, or add the report and Exhibit 15.','Company (Finance) / Ridgeline')

J='J. Signatures and Certifications'
add(J,'Section 302 certifications refer to an \"annual report\" - carried over from the 10-K template','Critical','Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2, paragraph 1',
 'Paragraph 1 of both certifications reads \"I have reviewed this annual report pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 of Verdana...\". The certification must identify the report being certified, here the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. The phrase \"pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d)...\" is not part of the prescribed text. Paragraph 4(d) should end \"; and\" (as in the Q2 2024 certifications), not with a period. The certification wording may not be altered except as Item 601(b)(31) permits.',
 'Exchange Act Rules 13a-14(a) and 15d-14(a); Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(31)(i) (prescribed exact form); SEC Release No. 33-8238; Q2 2024 Form 10-Q certifications (comparator).',
 'Revise paragraph 1 to: \"I have reviewed this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q of Verdana Industrial Technologies, Inc. for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2024;\". Conform paragraph 4(d) punctuation. Run a word-for-word comparison against Item 601(b)(31)(i) and the Q2 2024 certifications before execution.','Hargrove')
add(J,'Signature blocks and certification titles - conforming and execution items','Medium','Signature page; Exhibits 31.1-32.2',
 '(i) Signature and certification dates are blank (\"November __, 2024\"). They must be completed with the actual filing date, and Exhibits 31/32 must be dated no earlier than the date the officers review the final report. (ii) Officer titles are inconsistent: the signature page reads \"Chief Executive Officer and President (Principal Executive Officer)\", while the certifications read \"Chief Executive Officer\" and \"Chief Financial Officer\" without the principal-officer capacities. The Q2 2024 10-Q uses \"Chief Executive Officer and President\" and \"Chief Financial Officer (principal financial officer and principal accounting officer)\". (iii) Manually signed signature pages authenticating each typed /s/ signature must be obtained before filing and retained for five years.',
 'Form 10-Q signature requirements (signature by the registrant and by its principal financial officer or chief accounting officer); Exchange Act Rule 12b-11; Regulation S-T Rule 302(b) (retention of manually signed authentication documents); Item 601(b)(31) and (b)(32).',
 'Conform titles across the signature page and all four certifications to the Q2 2024 convention. Insert the filing date. Collect wet-ink or permitted electronic authentication documents under Rule 302(b) before EDGAR submission.','Hargrove / Company (Legal)')

add(A,"Target filing date of November 14, 2024 is after the statutory due date; Veterans Day premise is incorrect","Critical",

 "Form 10-Q, General Instruction A.1 (40 days after quarter-end for large accelerated filers); Exchange Act Rule 0-3(a) (a due date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or federal holiday moves to the next business day); Regulation S-T Rules 12 and 13 (EDGAR business days and hours; federal holidays excluded). Consequences of a late filing: loss of Form S-3 eligibility under General Instruction I.A.3(b) for 12 months (affecting the effective shelf, File No. 333-270815) and of well-known seasoned issuer status (Securities Act Rule 405); Rule 144(c)(1) current public information; NYSE Listed Company Manual Section 802.01E. A Rule 12b-25 notification (Form 12b-25 due by November 13, 2024; the 10-Q would then be due by Monday, November 18, 2024) is available only where the delay could not be eliminated without unreasonable effort or expense. A scheduling preference does not meet that standard.",
 "Reset the target filing date to no later than Tuesday, November 12, 2024. We recommend targeting Friday, November 8, 2024, with November 12 held as the fallback. Correct the “Statutory Deadline” entry in the Filing Metadata tab and the target date in the Checklist header. Fit the Audit Committee and Ridgeline sign-off to this schedule.  "Company (Legal/Finance); XBRL vendor; Hargrove")

add(D,"Note 3 (PolyShield) omits required ASC 805 interim disclosures","High","Note 3 – Business Combinations",
 "Note 3 gives the consideration and a condensed preliminary allocation, which foots: $123.8 million of assets less $31.1 million of liabilities equals $92.7 million, plus $72.3 million of goodwill equals $165.0 million.  "ASC 805-10-50-2 (including (h), acquiree revenue/earnings and pro forma information for public business entities) and 805-10-50-6; ASC 805-20-50-1; ASC 805-30-50-1 and 805-30-50-4; ASC 350-30-50-1; ASC 270-10-50-7; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant events since year-end). The General Counsel asked specifically for a complete ASC 805 interim disclosure.",
 "Expand Note 3 to cover items (a)–(i). Reconcile the $42.6 million intangible allocation to the Note 6 gross additions (see Finding 16). add(D,"Note 6 intangible asset amounts do not reconcile","High","Note 6 – Goodwill and Intangible Assets; balance sheet",
 "(i) Note 6 states that finite-lived intangibles plus $41.0 million of indefinite-lived trade names equal the balance-sheet totals at both dates. (ii) Gross carrying amounts increased $66.6 million (customer relationships +$38.3 million, technology +$26.7 million, other +$1.6 million), but the PolyShield allocation assigns only $42.6 million to intangibles. (iii) Accumulated amortization increased $33.2 million, but nine-month amortization expense is stated as $25.6 million. (iv) Intangibles on the balance sheet fall from $543.8 million to $518.2 million despite the $42.6 million acquisition. The goodwill roll-forward ($1,212.3 + $72.3 = $1,284.6 million) agrees.",
 "ASC 350-30-50-1 and 50-2; ASC 350-20-50-1; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5); Exchange Act Rule 12b-20.",

Extend the impairment-indicator statement to the nine-month period and address the class action and market capitalization.","Company (Finance) / Ridgeline")
add(D,"Note 5 maturity schedule inconsistent with term loan terms; amendment number unclear","Medium","Note 5 – Debt",
 "Note 5 says the August 20, 2024 amendment extended maturity from March 15, 2027 to August 20, 2029 but “did not modify the term loan facility.” If the term loan still matures on March 15, 2027, the maturity table should show a 2027 balloon payment of roughly $500 million or more, not $75.0 million.  "ASC 470-10-50-1 (maturities); Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5) (significant changes in long-term debt); Regulation S-K Item 303(b)(1).",

add(D,"Loss contingency disclosure for the securities class action is incomplete","High","Note 7 – Commitments and Contingencies (also Part II, Item 1)",
 "Note 7 describes the complaint but gives no ASC 450 assessment. The statement that the claims are “without merit” does not satisfy these requirements.",
 "ASC 450-20-50-3 to 50-5 (for a reasonably possible loss, the nature of the contingency and an estimate of possible loss or range, or a statement that such an estimate cannot be made); ASC 450-20-25-2; Regulation S-X Rule 10-01(a)(5).",
 "Subject to the views of Ridgeline and litigation counsel, add language such as: “The litigation is at an early stage. The Company has not recorded an accrual because a loss is not probable and reasonably estimable, and the Company is currently unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss, if any.” This meets the requirement without conceding liability. Add the class period and named plaintiff.","Company (Legal) / litigation counsel / Ridgeline")

 "ASC 280-10-50-32 (interim disclosure, for the current quarter and year-to-date, of segment revenues, segment profit or loss, material changes in segment assets, and a reconciliation of total segment profit or loss to consolidated income before income taxes).",
